notes: Baseline. War begins 27-28 Feb; strait still functioning normally at outset. ~17-18 mbpd total transit.
IRGC drone/tanker attacks begin in and around the strait; traffic disrupted but not formally closed.
IRGC destroys ~10 vessels attempting transit (4 Mar) and warns traffic prohibited; strait effectively shut. Insurance spikes 4-6x by 9 Mar.
New Supreme Leader vows to keep strait closed. Selective exceptions negotiated (Indian LNG tankers pass 14 Mar). ~3,200 vessels reported stranded west of strait (approx.).
Tehran: strait 'open to all except US and its allies'. Pakistani-flagged and select ships permitted. Stranded backlog persists (~3,200 vessels, approx.).
Iran pauses Hormuz traffic over Israeli attacks in Lebanon; ceasefire fraying.
Trump declares US naval blockade of the strait; CENTCOM enforces on Iranian-port traffic. Blockade formally starts 13 Apr.
Trump declares strait 'permanently open' (15 Apr); Iran says it reasserted control (18 Apr). Gunboat engagements and vessel seizures continue; contested control.
US 'Project Freedom' escorts US-flagged ships through; some transit resumes under convoy. Operation paused 6 May amid talks. Intermittent clashes.
Iran declares INDEFINITE closure (11 Jun). Transits collapse to ~5 ships/day vs 26 prior (21 Jun).
US-Iran agree to stop attacks (28 Jun); Islamabad Memorandum framework. Traffic partially eases during truce.
Iran strikes Qatari LNG tanker + others in Hormuz (7 Jul); truce violations mount; transit risk surges again.
IRGC navy closes strait 'until further notice' (11 Jul) after warning shot; further vessel damage.
US reinstates blockade and imposes 20% cargo toll ('Guardian of the Hormuz Strait'). Dataset ends 16 Jul with strait under militarized US control + Iranian contestation.
